title: Quick access tray shadow appears over taskbar and does not behave native (animation and clicking again)
author: CoennW
summary: The public report plus current runner code are enough to reproduce a plausible Quick Access tray-toggle bug locally, and the single-click path currently always reissues a show request instead of checking whether the flyout is already visible.

judgment.rationale: The issue already includes a video and a concrete click sequence, and a focused code pass shows a believable toggle flaw in the runner without needing the reporter to provide more logs first.
evidence: The report is on PowerToys 0.100.2 and includes a video of the tray-flyout shadow and close/reopen behavior.
runner/tray_icon.cpp routes every confirmed single left click to open_quick_access_flyout_window() when Quick Access is enabled.
runner/quick_access_host.cpp implements show() as start() plus SetEvent(show_event) with no current-state check or toggle path.

Common.UI.Controls/Window/FlyoutWindowHelper.cs positions flyout windows at the bottom-right work area edge and explicitly clamps size to avoid spilling into the taskbar, so a dark shadow over the taskbar points to runtime presentation behavior rather than raw placement math alone.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a targeted local reproduction on a current build, then design a runner/Quick Access toggle fix that does not re-show an already visible flyout and verifies shadow/animation behavior against the shared flyout host.

fix_assessment.rationale: There is no linked fix attempt, and current runner code exposes a concrete show-without-toggle path that matches the second-click symptom well enough to justify a maintainer reproduction and design.

proposed_fixes.title: Make tray single-click honor Quick Access visibility instead of always signaling show
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The runner currently treats every single left click as a show request. If the flyout is already open, the host receives another show signal instead of a hide/toggle command, which can produce the visible close-and-reopen behavior and interact badly with non-activating flyout presentation.
plan: Reproduce the issue on a current build while tracking Quick Access visibility and click flow.
Add an explicit visibility-aware toggle contract between tray_icon.cpp and the Quick Access host/UI so a second click hides an already open flyout instead of re-showing it.
Validate the resulting flyout shadow and entrance/exit behavior on the taskbar edge and mixed-focus scenarios.
verification: Single-click the tray icon with another window focused and confirm Quick Access opens once with the expected animation.
Single-click again while the flyout is still open and confirm it closes without an immediate reopen.

confidence.rationale: The runner-side toggle gap strongly matches the second-click symptom, but the shadow/animation behavior still needs a live repro to confirm whether the same change fully explains the visual artifact.

issue_context.summary: Quick Access appears visually non-native at the tray edge and reopens when the tray icon is clicked again, suggesting a runner/host visibility contract problem rather than a missing issue report.
known_information: The issue includes a direct video link and a concrete single-click repro on 0.100.2.
The reporter expects the flyout to behave like other Windows tray utilities, including second-click close behavior.
No assignee or linked fix is present.
The automated triage request for more steps did not add new public evidence.
inferences: The second-click symptom likely originates in the tray runner path, because it always reissues show and never branches on current flyout visibility.
The dark shadow over the taskbar may be a separate presentation bug, but it is best investigated in the same focused local repro because the flyout uses a shared window-positioning helper.
issue_context.analysis: A maintainer-side reproduce action is more useful than another reporter request. The issue already has a clear click path and media, while the remaining uncertainty is about internal visibility and rendering behavior.
initial_investigation: runner/tray_icon.cpp: click_timer_elapsed() always opens Quick Access on a single click when Quick Access is enabled.
runner/quick_access_host.cpp: QuickAccessHost::show() only starts the process and signals the show event; it does not track whether the flyout is already visible.
src/common/Common.UI.Controls/Window/FlyoutWindowHelper.cs already clamps bottom-right placement to the work area, so the taskbar-overlapping shadow is unlikely to be a simple size spill bug.

actions.label: Approve Quick Access tray toggle design
actions.note: Current hypothesis is strong enough to investigate locally, but the rendering symptom still needs live confirmation.

actions.label: Reproduce Quick Access tray toggle and shadow behavior
actions.note: Use the current build and watch whether the second click goes through a pure show path instead of hide/toggle.

prerequisites: Enable Quick Access so single left click opens the flyout from the tray icon.
Use a taskbar/dark-theme setup where the tray flyout shadow is easy to observe.
steps: Launch PowerToys with Quick Access enabled and focus another foreground window.
Single-click the PowerToys tray icon once and observe the flyout entrance animation and shadow relative to the taskbar edge.
Without moving focus elsewhere, single-click the same tray icon again while the flyout is still open.
Capture whether the second click closes the flyout cleanly or closes and immediately reopens it.
reproduce.expected_result: The first click opens Quick Access once with native-looking presentation, and the second click closes it without a close-and-reopen cycle.
